The latest 4-hour returns were negative (BTC −0.64%, ETH −0.87%), but the short windows are small and do not establish the direction of the next multi-day move.

Latest settled ETF data are mixed: BTC −185.4 reported units and ETH +2.3. Earlier calibration cohorts also included divergent or positive flows, which counter a uniformly negative-flow interpretation.
BTC funding is positive while ETH funding is negative; open interest declined modestly in both assets versus the previous capture. This is not a uniform leverage signal.

Rotation measures remain between published thresholds across 30-, 90- and 365-day BlockchainCenter horizons; the 90-day score rose from 35 to 39, while the 30-day score stayed at 33. These are shadow measures, not canonical cycle confirmation.

BTC and ETH CFGI readings are both classified Fear (scores 24 and 31). The 4-hour scores rose slightly versus the prior capture, but sentiment remains weak.

Over the API 70-hour window, net aggressive quote flow was negative for BTC and ETH, alongside negative returns. Latest captured spot taker imbalances were also negative for both, though captured trade windows and depth snapshots are short-lived.

The Action Compass calibration artifact reports low-confidence retest-risk observations in earlier cohorts and substantial subsequent downside in some 72-hour and 168-hour no-warning samples. It is descriptive only; overlapping freezes are not independent events and this does not validate a current warning or forecast.

Persistent ETH/BTC weakness and poor proxy breadth may be accompanying the price decline; the supplied material does not establish that either leads or causes further downside.
The short-window bounce may represent stabilization or a temporary interruption in the decline; subsequent breadth, ETH/BTC and settled-flow observations would distinguish these possibilities.

The dataset does not establish whether the latest rebound will persist.
